headline: Wall Street closes in a correction, and the first crack appears in December hike pricing

findings.headline: The S&P 500 ends the week in a correction as the Anthropic listing fails to revive the AI trade
findings.body: AP says the index is now more than 10% below its 6 October record, its first correction since March 2025, after its worst week since April 2025, and the Nasdaq has given back all of this year's gain. Anthropic's IPO prompted profit-taking across AI names rather than fresh buying. Leading and lagging was textbook defensive: consumer staples and health care held up while tech and chips lagged on both sides of the Atlantic.

sources.label: AP: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq goes negative for the year

findings.headline: Fed futures start to doubt a December hike, even as the Fed keeps talking tough
findings.body: CME FedWatch now gives a 7.9% chance of a hold on 9 December, from zero on Thursday, and has dropped the 50bp option that stood at 6.1%, although a 25bp hike is still about 92% priced. That shift came on a day when Governor Lisa Cook said broad inflation needs a more aggressive response, and two days after Governor Waller argued for 50bp. LPL's Lawrence Gillum notes the Fed has room to slow down if the AI sell-off tightens financial conditions, and that is what futures have started to price.

findings.headline: Gold and silver are being sold to cover equity losses, not as a haven
findings.body: High Ridge Futures says the AI sell-off is forcing liquidation of gold positions, and Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson's warning on inflation added rate pressure, leaving spot gold at a 14-month low and heading for its worst week in eight months. Spot silver is now about 66% below January's record. While bonds rallied, metals behaved like a source of cash, so the CFTC positioning is worth watching for signs that the forced selling has run its course.

sources.label: CNBC: Gold's slide deepens as AI rout, rate hike bets hurt bullion

view: Our view: Friday turned an AI-led de-risking into a broader liquidation, with precious metals sold alongside chips while Treasuries got the haven bid. The early sign that futures doubt a December hike matters more than the close: October PCE on Wednesday 25 November at 14:30 Zurich, the day before Thanksgiving, decides whether that doubt grows into relief for growth stocks or the hike gets locked back in.
